options.plan: Upstream release 26.8.0; upstream workforce entitlement and commercial support unverified
options.region: Operator-selected hosting and upstream tenant; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Realm-scoped generic OIDC broker, fixed Entra workforce tenant v2 issuer; first-login JIT; no SCIM pairing verified

conditions: Select a realm-scoped generic OIDC broker using Authorization Code, client authentication, an exact issuer and signature validation with the matching JWKS; this is a protocol-based proposal, not vendor-certified or runtime-tested interoperability.

Register a confidential Entra Web app with the broker callback and a fixed workforce Tenant ID; use tenant-specific v2 discovery per https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-protocols-oidc and code-flow credentials per https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow. Common, Organizations, Consumers, External ID and B2C are outside this selected scope.

Only the Keycloak source is release-pinned; upstream documentation is mutable and dated. Upstream workforce entitlements, hosting costs and commercial support remain unverified; this is not a zero-cost guarantee or a change to AuthWeave authentication.

evidence.summary: The pinned broker guide documents generic OIDC code-flow configuration and issuer/signature checks. Selecting a fixed Entra workforce tenant is a conditional protocol-based proposal, not a verified pair.

conditions: Enable Create User If Unique in the selected first broker login flow; local user creation and identity linking occur at login, not through background provisioning, and can be disabled independently of realm self-registration.

Review profile requirements, identifier collisions and proof of control for existing accounts; do not enable unverified automatic email-based linking. Login-time JIT does not establish SCIM deactivation or consuming-app session revocation.

evidence.summary: The first-login flow can create a unique local user or require verification when linking an existing account. Its automatic-linking warning prevents interpreting JIT as safe unconditional account matching or lifecycle synchronization.

conditions: Native realm SCIM server support does not verify this Entra provisioning pair: endpoint authorization, upstream entitlement, identity correlation with the brokered user and operation compatibility still need pair-specific evidence and tests. UNKNOWN is not UNAVAILABLE.

Do not inherit native SCIM OPTIONAL or Auth0-specific oid/objectId/externalId mappings into this generic OIDC scope; use a separate reviewed provisioning configuration and establish how the brokered identity correlates with provisioned resources.
Inbound provisioning into Keycloak is not outbound SaaS provisioning; deactivation, authorization and consuming-app session enforcement remain separate and untested.

evidence.summary: The release documents a realm-scoped SCIM server for external provisioners. It does not establish Entra entitlement, broker/SCIM identity correlation or a tested provisioning configuration for this selected login scope.

conditions: OIDC claim mappers import or update data at login according to sync mode; Entra group claims and application assignment do not establish background group lifecycle or deprovisioning.

Native SCIM Group resources are a separate interface, not proof of this pair; group membership, deletion, nested-group behavior and downstream SaaS permissions require separate evidence. No external bridge is selected.

evidence.summary: Broker mappers describe first-login import and repeated-login updates. This does not establish group lifecycle synchronization from Entra or enforcement in a consuming application.
